html: The Moratoc were a people of the lower Roanoke River in northeastern North Carolina in the late 1500s. They are known mainly from the accounts of the English Roanoke colony. In 1586 its governor, Ralph Lane, led a party up the river into their country in search of copper and pearls, but the Moratoc had left their villages and the English found no food. The colony's reports even called the river the Moratoc. Their language and later fate are uncertain; they probably merged with neighbours such as the Chowanoke or Secotan.
